mainTopic: How a person's intention (מחשבה) shapes liability for הוצאה on שבת: storing an item for its use, the minimum amount for seeds, whether one person's storing can obligate someone else, and changing one's mind mid-act.
overview: This amud continues the גמרא on the משנה about someone who stored a small item and later carried it out on שבת. First the גמרא explains that he is liable because a person acts on his original plan. Then רב יהודה in the name of שמואל says רבי מאיר makes a person liable even for one wheat kernel carried out for planting. רב יצחק בריה דרב יהודה challenges this with the case of someone who plans to carry out his whole house, and the גמרא answers that a strange plan nobody else shares is ignored. The גמרא then notes that the משנה's rule, that anyone else needs the normal measure, disagrees with רבי שמעון בן אלעזר, who holds that one person's storing can make another person liable. רבא in the name of רב נחמן rules that switching between eating and planting while carrying does not cancel liability. רבא then builds a ladder of questions about seeds that swelled or shrank along the way, and all of them end in תיקו. Finally רבא asks רב נחמן whether an olive-size of תרומה that completes an egg-size of impure food counts for שבת. רב נחמן begins answering from אבא שאול's ruling on the Temple breads, and the argument finishes on the next amud.

steps.title: A person acts on his original plan
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes explaining why the משנה needed to say that one who stored an item and later carried it out is liable: he still acts based on his original reason for storing it.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have thought that he totally canceled his original intention. So the משנה teaches us: anyone who does something does it based on his first intention.
steps.whatsHappening: This finishes an answer that began earlier. The גמרא explains what the משנה adds by saying that one who stored a tiny item and later carried it out is liable for any amount.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Maybe when he carries it out later, he is not thinking about why he stored it, so his old plan should not count. The משנה teaches that his original intention stays in force. That is why the small item still counts as important to him.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said (introduces a mistaken assumption)

steps.whyThisMatters: The idea that a person's earlier plan carries forward into his later action is the foundation for the rest of this passage, which keeps asking how much a person's intention matters.

phrases.english: Lest you say
that he completely nullified his intention
it teaches us:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל הָעוֹשֶׂה, עַל דַּעַת רִאשׁוֹנָה הוּא עוֹשֶׂה.
phrases.english: anyone who acts, acts with the original intention in mind.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer to the question asked on the previous amud, about why the משנה needed to say he is liable.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains the חידוש: it rules out the idea that his intention was canceled.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: His storing intention was forgotten and canceled by the time he carried it out.
steps.terutzMaskana: A person acts based on his original intention, so he is liable.

steps.title: Even one wheat kernel makes one liable
steps.stepSummary: שמואל teaches that רבי מאיר makes a person liable even for carrying out a single wheat kernel meant for planting.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: רבי מאיר made a person liable even for carrying out one wheat kernel for planting.
steps.whatsHappening: A new statement: according to רבי מאיר, carrying one single kernel of wheat for planting is enough to be liable.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually carrying requires a set minimum amount. Here שמואל says that for someone who wants to plant, even one kernel counts, because one kernel can be planted.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
Rabbi Meir would deem liable
even one who carries out a single wheat kernel for sowing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic: the minimum amount for seeds meant for planting.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי מאיר, carrying out even one wheat kernel for planting makes a person liable.

steps.title: Isn't that obvious from the משנה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why שמואל needed to say this, since the משנה already says 'any amount'.
steps.simpleTranslation: That's obvious! We learned 'any amount' in the משנה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges שמואל's statement as unnecessary, because the משנה already says a person is liable for 'any amount'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An unattributed משנה follows רבי מאיר. If the משנה says 'any amount', of course one kernel counts. So what is שמואל adding?

phrases.english: It is obvious; we learned 'any amount'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges step 2 as adding nothing new.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה already says 'any amount', so saying 'one kernel' adds nothing.

steps.title: 'Any amount' could have meant an olive-size
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that 'any amount' might have meant only less than the usual food measure while still requiring an olive-size. שמואל teaches that it really means even one kernel.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said that 'any amount' only means to exclude the size of a dried fig, but really you still need at least an olive's size. So שמואל teaches us otherwise.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains what שמואל adds: without him, we might have read 'any amount' in a limited way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The usual measure for carrying food is a כגרוגרת (dried fig). We might have thought 'any amount' only lowers that to a smaller measure, a כזית (olive). שמואל teaches that even a single kernel is enough.

keyTerms.meaning: Dried fig (the usual measure for carrying food)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the sizes: a כזית (olive) is SMALLER than a גרוגרת (dried fig). The mistaken reading lowered the measure only part of the way, from fig-size to olive-size.

phrases.english: Lest you say:
'any amount' is meant to exclude a dried fig-bulk,
but really not until there is an olive-bulk,
he teaches us otherwise.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַהוּ דְּתֵימָא: כׇּל שֶׁהוּא — לְאַפּוֹקֵי מִגְּרוֹגֶרֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא in step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Clarifies the wording of the משנה by ruling out a narrower reading.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Any amount' means less than a גרוגרת but at least a כזית.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Any amount' truly means even one kernel.

steps.title: What about planning to carry out his whole house?
steps.stepSummary: רב יצחק בריה דרב יהודה objects: if a person's intention sets his measure, then someone who planned to carry out his whole house should not be liable until he carries out all of it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יצחק the son of רב יהודה challenged this: But according to this, if someone planned to carry out his whole house, would he not be liable until he carries out all of it?!
steps.whatsHappening: רב יצחק pushes the idea of 'personal intention sets the measure' to an extreme to show a problem with it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If one kernel counts because this person considers it important, then intention seems to control the measure in both directions. Someone who decided he only cares about moving his whole house would then be exempt for anything less, which sounds absurd.

phrases.aramaic: מַתְקִיף לַהּ רַב יִצְחָק בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוּדָה:
phrases.english: Rav Yitzchak son of Rav Yehuda objected to this:

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא מֵעַתָּה, חִישֵּׁב לְהוֹצִיא כׇּל בֵּיתוֹ,
phrases.english: But now, if he planned to carry out his entire house,
so too would he not be liable
until he carries out all of it?!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקִיף לַהּ רַב יִצְחָק בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוּדָה: אֶלָּא מֵעַתָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the logic behind steps 2 and 4: that personal intention defines the measure.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that a person's own intention sets his measure for liability
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Reductio ad absurdum: if intention can lower the measure, it should also be able to raise it, which is absurd.

steps.title: An unusual plan is ignored
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that a plan to carry out a whole house is so unusual that it does not count against the way everyone else behaves.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, his intention is canceled in light of what all people do.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers רב יצחק by separating the two cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Planting one kernel is a real, normal use, so that intention counts. Wanting to move only a whole house at once is so strange that the law ignores it and uses the normal measure everyone uses. Intention can make a small thing significant, but it cannot cancel what ordinary people treat as significant.
steps.whatToRemember: A person's intention can make a small amount significant, like one kernel for planting. But a bizarre intention that no normal person shares is ignored, and the standard measure applies.

phrases.aramaic: הָתָם — בָּטְלָה דַּעְתּוֹ אֵצֶל כׇּל אָדָם.
phrases.english: There, his intention is nullified relative to all other people.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָתָם — בָּטְלָה דַּעְתּוֹ אֵצֶל כׇּל אָדָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא in step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishes the cases: a normal intention versus an abnormal one.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Intention controls the measure in every case.
steps.terutzMaskana: A strange intention that goes against common practice is ignored.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה: others need the normal measure
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה: anyone else who carries out the stored item is liable only for the normal measure.
steps.simpleTranslation: And any other person is liable for it only if he carries out its normal measure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next words of the משנה to set up a comment about them. This step is setting up the next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says the special 'any amount' rule applies only to the person who stored the item. Anyone else who carries it out needs the standard measure, because the storer's intention is not his.

phrases.english: And any other person is not liable for it
except for its standard measure.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכׇל אָדָם אֵין חַיָּיבִין עָלָיו אֶלָּא כְּשִׁיעוּרוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to a new line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Someone other than the storer is liable only for the standard measure.

steps.title: The משנה disagrees with רבי שמעון בן אלעזר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says this line of the משנה does not follow רבי שמעון בן אלעזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Our משנה is not according to רבי שמעון בן אלעזר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא identifies a תנא who disagrees with this line of the משנה. The proof comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the משנה says others need the full measure, it must hold that the storer's intention does not affect anyone else. The גמרא is about to show that רבי שמעון בן אלעזר holds the opposite.

phrases.aramaic: מַתְנִיתִין דְּלָא כְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר,
phrases.english: The mishna is not in accordance with Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar,

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִיתִין דְּלָא כְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Comments on the line of the משנה quoted in step 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The line 'others need the normal measure' does not follow רבי שמעון בן אלעזר.

steps.title: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר: one person's storing obligates another
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows that רבי שמעון בן אלעזר holds that if one person stored an unusual item, anyone else who carries it out is liable because of the storer's intention.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר stated a rule. Anything that is not fit to store, and people do not store things like it, but it became fit for this person and he stored it, and then someone else came and carried it out: the second person is liable because of the first person's intention.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to prove that רבי שמעון בן אלעזר disagrees with our משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי שמעון בן אלעזר, once someone stored the item, it becomes a significant object for everyone, so even another person who carries it out is liable. Our משנה says only the storer gets the special rule, and others need the normal measure. So the two clearly disagree.
steps.whyThisMatters: This raises a basic question: does a person's intention only change his own liability, or can it change the status of the object itself for everyone?

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא: כְּלָל אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר,
phrases.english: as it was taught: Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar stated a principle:
anything that is not fit to be stored,
and people do not store things like it,
but it became fit for this person and he stored it,
and another person came and carried it out,
this one is liable through the intention of that one.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: כְּלָל אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source for the claim in step 8.
steps.raayaObject: That our משנה does not follow רבי שמעון בן אלעזר
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא quoting רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's general rule

steps.title: Changing one's mind between eating and planting
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן rules that someone who carried out a fig-size amount for eating and switched to planting, or the reverse, is liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said in the name of רב נחמן: If someone carried out a dried fig's amount to eat, and changed his mind to plant it, or carried it out to plant and changed his mind to eat it, he is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: A new ruling: changing your purpose during the act of carrying does not exempt you.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A כגרוגרת is enough for liability whether the purpose is eating or planting. So switching between the two purposes still leaves a full measure either way.

phrases.english: Rava said that Rav Nachman said:
If one carried out a dried fig-bulk for eating,
and changed his mind about it, deciding to plant it;
or alternatively, if he carried it out for planting,
and changed his mind to eat it, he is liable.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new case about a change of intention.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Switching between eating and planting midway does not exempt someone who carried out a fig-size amount.

steps.title: Isn't that obvious, since either way there is a measure?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רב נחמן needed to say this, since both purposes have a full measure.
steps.simpleTranslation: That's obvious! Go this way, there is a measure; go that way, there is a measure!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב נחמן's ruling as unnecessary.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Whether you look at his first plan or his final plan, a כגרוגרת is enough to be liable. So of course he is liable. What is the חידוש?

keyTerms.meaning: Go this way, look at it from this side

phrases.english: It is obvious: go this way, there is a measure;
and go that way, there is a measure!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges step 10 as adding nothing new.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both intentions come with a full measure, so liability seems obvious.

steps.title: Lifting and placing need not share one intention
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that we might have required the lifting and the placing to be done with the same intention. רב נחמן teaches that this is not needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said that we need the lifting and the placing to be done with one intention, and here that is missing. So he teaches us that he is still liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the חידוש of רב נחמן's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Carrying is made of two parts: עקירה (lifting the object) and הנחה (placing it down). Here he lifted it with one purpose and placed it with another, so we might think it splits into two half-acts. רב נחמן teaches that it is still one complete act, and he is liable.

keyTerms.meaning: Lifting the object from its place

steps.whatToRemember: Carrying on שבת needs both עקירה and הנחה, but they do not need the same purpose. If both purposes come with a full measure, changing your mind between lifting and placing still makes you liable.

phrases.english: Lest you say
we require lifting and placing with one intention
and that is not present here,
he teaches us otherwise.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַהוּ דְּתֵימָא בָּעֵינַן עֲקִירָה וְהַנָּחָה בַּחֲדָא מַחְשָׁבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא in step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains the חידוש by ruling out a mistaken requirement.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Lifting and placing must share one intention, otherwise there is no complete act.
steps.terutzMaskana: A change of intention between lifting and placing does not split the act, so he is liable.

steps.title: Half a fig-size for planting that swelled, then switched to eating
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks about seeds taken out for planting at less than a גרוגרת, which swelled to a full גרוגרת before he decided to eat them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא asked: Someone carried out half a dried-fig amount of seeds to plant them. They swelled up, and then he changed his mind and decided to eat them. What is the law? One side: In רב נחמן's case he is liable, because whichever purpose you look at, there was a full measure. But here, when he carried it out, it was not big enough to count for eating, so he should not be liable. Other side: If he had kept quiet and never changed his mind, he would be liable based on his planting plan. So now too he should be liable.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא takes רב נחמן's ruling one step further and asks a new 'what if' question. He lays out the reasons for both possible answers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Seeds count for planting even in a tiny amount, but for eating you need a full גרוגרת. When carried out, it was big enough for planting but not for eating. The question is whether the new eating plan cancels the liability, or whether the original planting plan still holds him liable.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked a question he did not know the answer to (a dilemma)
Half the size of a dried fig, which is less than the measure for food
If you want to say (one side of a dilemma)
He kept quiet, meaning he never changed his plan

steps.confusionAlert: The phrase 'אם תמצי לומר' here just opens the first side of the question. It is not yet the start of the next-level question. That use comes in the next step.

phrases.english: Rava asked:
If he carried out half a dried-fig amount for planting, and it swelled,
and he changed his mind about it, deciding to eat it, what is the law?

phrases.aramaic: אִם תִּמְצֵי לוֹמַר: הָתָם הוּא דְּמִיחַיַּיב —
phrases.english: You could say: there (in Rav Nachman's case) he is liable,
phrases.notes: This is the first side of the question.

phrases.english: because go this way, there is a full measure,
and go that way, there is a full measure,
but here, since at the time he carried it out

phrases.aramaic: לָא הֲוָה בֵּיהּ שִׁיעוּר אֲכִילָה — לָא מִיחַיַּיב,
phrases.english: it did not have the measure for eating, he is not liable,
or perhaps: since if he had kept quiet
phrases.notes: And here's the other side of the question.

phrases.english: and had not thought anything new about it,
he would be liable on account of the planting intention,
now too he is liable.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends רב נחמן's switching-intention ruling to a case where the size changed in between.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does a later eating intention cancel liability when the item lacked the eating measure at the time it was carried out, but had the planting measure?

steps.title: A fig-size for eating that shrank, then switched to planting
steps.stepSummary: Assuming he is liable in the first case, רבא asks about the reverse: food that shrank below a גרוגרת and was then switched to planting.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say he is liable because the original planting plan would have made him liable anyway, then what about this: he carried out a full dried-fig amount to eat, it shrank, and then he decided to plant it. What is the law? Here, if he had kept quiet, his original eating plan would certainly not make him liable, since it shrank. Or perhaps we go by his plan right now, and he is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא climbs one rung up the ladder. He assumes the answer to his first question was 'liable' and asks a harder version.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason for 'liable' in step 13 was 'his original plan would have made him liable anyway.' That reason does not work here, because after shrinking, the eating plan would no longer make him liable. So the only way to make him liable is to follow his current planting plan.

keyTerms.meaning: The first intention, his original plan
We go according to now, the present situation

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם תִּמְצֵי לוֹמַר: כֵּיוָן דְּאִילּוּ אִישְׁתִּיק
phrases.english: And if you say: since if he had kept quiet

phrases.aramaic: וְלָא חַשֵּׁיב עֲלֵיהּ מִיחַיַּיב אַמַּחְשָׁבָה דִזְרִיעָה,
phrases.english: and had not thought anything new, he would be liable on account of the planting intention,
now too he is liable,
then if he carried out a dried-fig amount for eating, and it shrank,
and he changed his mind about it, deciding to plant it, what is the law?
Here, certainly, if he had kept quiet,
he would not be liable on account of the first intention,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִילְמָא בָּתַר הַשְׁתָּא אָזְלִינַן, וּמִיחַיַּיב.
phrases.english: or perhaps we go according to now, and he is liable.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A follow-up question that assumes 'liable' as the answer to step 13.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: When the original intention can no longer create liability, do we follow the present intention instead?

steps.title: Food that shrank and then swelled back
steps.stepSummary: Assuming we follow the present, רבא asks about food that shrank below a גרוגרת and then grew back. Does the in-between shrinking disqualify it?
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say we go according to now and he is liable, then what about this: he carried out a dried-fig amount to eat, it shrank, and then it swelled back up. What is the law? Is there 'pushing away' (permanent disqualification) for the laws of שבת, or is there no 'pushing away' for the laws of שבת?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא climbs to the top rung of his ladder. He asks whether a temporary drop below the measure permanently ruins liability, even though the item went back to full size.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here his intention never changed. Only the size dipped in the middle. The question is whether the concept of דיחוי applies to שבת: once something is 'pushed off' from counting, can it come back?

keyTerms.meaning: It went back and swelled again
Being 'pushed away,' a disqualification that may be permanent

steps.confusionAlert: דיחוי is a known concept elsewhere (for example in קרבנות). רבא is asking whether that same idea works for carrying on שבת. He is not assuming it does.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם תִּמְצֵי לוֹמַר: בָּתַר הַשְׁתָּא אָזְלִינַן, וּמִיחַיַּיב —
phrases.english: And if you say: we go according to now, and he is liable,
then if he carried out a dried-fig amount for eating,
and it shrank and then swelled back, what is the law?
Is there disqualification ('pushing away') regarding Shabbat,
or is there no disqualification regarding Shabbat?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִם תִּמְצֵי לוֹמַר: בָּתַר הַשְׁתָּא אָזְלִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The final follow-up, assuming 'we follow the present' from step 14.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the principle of דיחוי apply to the measures for carrying on שבת?

steps.title: The questions stay unresolved
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא leaves all of רבא's dilemmas unanswered: תיקו.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let it stand (unresolved).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes this ladder of questions without an answer. They remain open.
steps.deeperAnalysis: תיקו means no source was found to decide any of the questions. The whole chain of 'what ifs' is left as a real doubt.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it stand. The question stays unresolved

steps.whatToRemember: רבא built a ladder of three questions: small-then-grew with switching, big-then-shrank with switching, and shrank-then-grew back (דיחוי). All end in תיקו.

phrases.english: Let it stand (unresolved).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the dilemmas of steps 13 to 15.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: All of רבא's dilemmas about changing size and intention remain undecided.

steps.title: Throwing an olive-size of תרומה into an impure house
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks רב נחמן about someone who threw an olive-size of תרומה into an impure house.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא asked רב נחמן: If someone threw an olive-size of תרומה into an impure house, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: A new question begins. רבא asks רב נחמן about an olive-size of תרומה thrown into an impure house, but the question is not yet clear.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question as stated is short and puzzling. The גמרא will first have to figure out what exactly is being asked.

keyTerms.meaning: The portion of produce given to a כהן
A house that is ritually impure

phrases.english: Rava asked of Rav Nachman:

phrases.aramaic: זָרַק כְּזַיִת תְּרוּמָה לְבַיִת טָמֵא מַהוּ?
phrases.english: If one threw an olive-size of teruma into an impure house, what is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new question about measures, now involving impurity.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is the law when an olive-size of תרומה is thrown into an impure house?

steps.title: An olive-size seems too small for either issue
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the question is about: an olive-size is too small both for שבת (a גרוגרת) and for food impurity (a כביצה).
steps.simpleTranslation: About what? If it is about שבת, we need a dried-fig amount. If it is about impurity, food needs an egg-size!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the question itself. It seems an olive-size cannot matter for anything here.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On שבת, carrying food needs a גרוגרת, and a כזית is smaller. Food only becomes impure when it is a כביצה, and a כזית is smaller too. So the question seems pointless either way.

keyTerms.meaning: An egg-size amount, the measure for food to become impure

phrases.english: About what?
If regarding Shabbat, we require a dried-fig amount;

phrases.aramaic: אִי לְעִנְיַן טוּמְאָה — כְּבֵיצָה אוֹכָלִין בָּעֵינַן!
phrases.english: if regarding impurity, we require an egg-size of food!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the meaning of רבא's question.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A כזית falls short of both the שבת measure and the impurity measure, so the question seems to have no subject.

steps.title: It is about שבת, and the olive completes an egg-size
steps.stepSummary: The question is about שבת, in a case where the house already has less than a כביצה of food, and this כזית brings it up to a כביצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really, it is about שבת. The case is where there was already less than an egg-size of food in the house, and this olive-size completes it to an egg-size.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by spelling out the exact case behind רבא's question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By itself the כזית is too small. But together with the food already in the house, it creates a כביצה that can become impure. So the כזית does matter for impurity, and the question is whether that also matters for שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: For example, in a case where

phrases.english: Actually, it is regarding Shabbat,
and the case is where there is less than an egg-size of food,
and this completes it to an egg-size.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 18 by defining the case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: An olive-size has no significance for שבת or impurity.
steps.terutzMaskana: It has significance for impurity when it completes a כביצה, so the question is about שבת in that setting.

steps.title: Does counting for impurity make it count for שבת?
steps.stepSummary: The clarified dilemma: since the כזית counts toward impurity, is he liable on שבת, or does שבת always need a גרוגרת?
steps.simpleTranslation: So what is the law? Since it joins together for impurity, is he also liable for שבת? Or perhaps everything on שבת needs a dried-fig amount?
steps.whatsHappening: Now that the case is clear, the גמרא states רבא's real question in full.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One side says: the item has real importance, since it completes an impurity measure, so carrying it should count on שבת. The other side says: שבת has its own fixed measure, a גרוגרת, and other areas of law do not change it.

keyTerms.meaning: Joins together, combines toward a measure

phrases.english: What is the law? Since it joins together regarding impurity,
is he also liable regarding Shabbat,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִילְמָא: כׇּל לְעִנְיַן שַׁבָּת כִּגְרוֹגֶרֶת בָּעֵינַן?
phrases.english: or perhaps: for everything regarding Shabbat we require a dried-fig amount?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Restates רבא's dilemma now that the case has been defined.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Can importance under the laws of impurity create liability on שבת below the standard גרוגרת measure?

steps.title: רב נחמן cites אבא שאול on the Temple breads
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן says the answer was already taught: אבא שאול rules that the measure for שתי הלחם and לחם הפנים is a גרוגרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: You already learned it. אבא שאול says: For the two loaves and the showbread, the measure is a dried-fig amount.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן answers רבא by pointing to a ברייתא. He will show that this teaching settles the question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These are holy Temple breads, which also have their own measure under the laws of טומאה. Even so, אבא שאול gives them the normal שבת measure of a גרוגרת. This suggests that a measure from another area of law does not change the שבת measure. The next step begins spelling out the argument.

keyTerms.meaning: You have already learned it (in a ברייתא)
The two loaves brought on שבועות
The showbread in the בית המקדש

phrases.english: He said to him: You learned it.
Abba Shaul says:
The two loaves and the showbread,
their measure is a dried-fig amount,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: רב נחמן responds to רבא's dilemma with a source.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The שבת measure stays a גרוגרת even for items that have a different measure under other laws such as טומאה, as shown from אבא שאול.

steps.title: Why the ברייתא proves the point
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins explaining the proof: why does אבא שאול not take the measure these breads have in another area of law (impurity) and apply it to שבת? The sentence continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: And why? Let us say: since regarding...
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא starts asking why אבא שאול did not use the impurity measure for שבת. The argument finishes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is rhetorical. It suggests that we might have linked the שבת measure to the impurity measure. The fact that אבא שאול did not do so will be the proof for רבא's question.
steps.confusionAlert: Although it looks like a challenge, this question is part of רב נחמן's proof. It is not an attack on the ברייתא.

phrases.english: And why?
Let us say: since regarding...
phrases.notes: The sentence continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins drawing the inference from אבא שאול's ruling.
steps.raayaObject: That the שבת measure is not borrowed from impurity rules
steps.raayaSupportSource: אבא שאול's ברייתא about שתי הלחם and לחם הפנים
